A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison despite extensive layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-denoising, text-classification, and Llama fine-tuning experiments, including robustness evaluations and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds RoBERTa evaluations under uniform embedding noise and discrete text corruption.

M1.justification: The descent-constrained objective, primal-dual updates, resilient relaxation, and architecture adaptations remain unchanged. Explicit nonnegative initialization in Algorithm 1 and corrected attention indices clarify the existing formulation.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 adds uniform embedding noise and random character replacement plus word deletion on IMDb. These extend input-condition coverage beyond Gaussian noise; the datasets and underlying tasks are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set remains unchanged, and the added tests compare constrained with unconstrained RoBERTa. RoBERTa–MNLI already appears in v1 Figure 4 and Table 4 despite contradictory omission statements, so its presence in v2 is not a new comparison.

E3.justification: The new tests introduce uniform noise sampled from U(−√3γ, √3γ) and simultaneous character-replacement and word-deletion procedures controlled by probability p. Retained experiments largely preserve their documented splits, metrics, budgets, and settings; changed plots alone do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: New Section 4.1 and Figures 4–5 test whether robustness extends beyond Gaussian embedding perturbations to uniform noise and discrete textual corruption. Existing depth, hyperparameter, constraint-satisfaction, failure-case, and completion analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-run selection in Appendix B.3 and three-seed ablations with uncertainty displays in Appendix B.6. The new robustness plots introduce no additional uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds uniform-noise and text-corruption results; Figure 5 shows approximately 0.66 versus 0.52 accuracy at p = 0.30. Existing Gaussian classification curves also change in Figure 1 and v1 Figure 4/v2 Figure 2. Appendix B.4 corrects a 71% RMSE reduction to 47.9% for unchanged values of 14.724 versus 28.269. Tables 3–4 retain their numerical entries.

T1.justification: The convergence and distribution-shift guarantees, Assumptions 1–7, and derivations in Appendices A and C are retained. Index corrections and theorem-heading edits do not substantively revise the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The introduction's text-classification contribution explicitly expands robustness claims to uniform embedding noise and random textual perturbations. The central constrained-training, convergence, and generalization contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds an argument for negligible training overhead and interprets discrete corruptions as approximations to OCR or transcription errors. The conclusion adds prospective applications involving neural algorithmic reasoning, diffusion, and latent reasoning. Existing feasibility failures and per-sample limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code URL in the abstract and explains activation reuse and multiplier-memory scaling. Existing hardware, libraries, hyperparameters, and fine-tuning details are retained. The PDFs establish the new access information, not the repository's contents or availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds He and Vitercik on primal-dual neural algorithmic reasoning, Hounie et al. on forecasting constraints, and Khalafi et al. on constrained diffusion. These modestly broaden positioning; numerous other reference edits update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The empirical narrative changes from video–text–LLM to text–LLM–video. v2 adds a robustness subsection, overhead discussion, expanded conclusion, acknowledgements, and impact statement, alongside local copy edits. Most existing prose and appendix exposition are retained.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to a two-column conference layout, substantially resizing and repositioning figures and equations. Classification panels receive revised labels and legends, two robustness figures are added, and Tables 4–5 move to the document's end. Several formerly wide plots become small single-column displays.

improvement.justification: The new tests provide useful evidence that robustness extends beyond Gaussian embedding noise, while the code-access information and corrected RMSE percentage improve reproducibility information and accuracy. These are limited gains: the method and theory remain unchanged, some existing curves change without explanation, and several plots become less legible.
